raw_tweets.text:
This is scary.

I downloaded an uncensored version of Qwen 3.8 27B onto my Mac

It literally does anything you want. First prompt I gave it was asking how you make meth. It immediately answered.

With all the noise about slowing down AI innovation in order to increase safety, what is even the point if after every release we'll get an open source version with 0 safety guards?

Opus 4.6 level intelligence with 0 alignment that will do anything you want.

We are coming up with all these rules and regulations, slowing down companies, making it harder to release models. But then the moment a model releases it gets distilled and uncensored

I don't know what the solution to this is. You can't ban open source. That will be impossible. People will find ways online to find the files

You can't ban uncensored models. Would be too difficult to enforce. And again, people will get around it

Do you just stop putting the breaks on companies knowing it doesn't matter? I mean this is literally a model that can run on a laptop. I'd estimate at least half of Americans can run this model.

I don't know what the answer. I 100% believe safety is a priority and it's dangerous to have this technology in the wrong hands.

But how do you enforce safety when safety is becoming increasingly difficult to maintain?

If safety becomes impossible to maintain, do you still prioritize it?

I'd argue this is the number one issue going into the next election.

quoted_tweet.text:
Goodbye mental load....hellooooo @bot !

I know, I know. Grok Bot seems like it must be the next new thing for tech bros cold plunging in Patagonia vests, but hear me out moms (yes moms because disproportionately, the mental load falls more on moms than dads).

Offload that mental load to AI and watch things just get done.

Is it perfect? No.
Is it amazing? Absolutely.

Grok Bot is the new AI assistant from the team at Cursor + SpaceX (they're calling it SpaceXai). It's surprisingly useful and easy for non-technical people to use, and it can do a whole heck of a lot more than Claude and ChatGPT with little to no setup. 

Here are actual things that Grok Bot did for me this week (almost completely independently):

- Looked through back to school emails and made sure I was prepared with everything that needed to be done for multiple kids. 

Mental load unlock: 100% I would've forgotten to pack a space change of clothes for my kindergartner on her first day.

- Found 3 gift cards I somehow forgot to use from the last year. Oh right, I DID buy 2 Gap gift cards from Costco on black friday! Duh.

Mental load unlock: Cha-ching! That's $150 in my pocket.

- Scheduled multiple appointments for me. I've been putting off my annual physical exam because who has time to call the doctor. Grok Bot looked up options, pinged me with 3 dates/times, then booked it (I just had to confirm Zocdoc on the last step). It created a calendar reminder!

Mental load unlock: Moms, we often put off our own health/wellbeing. Finally! AI can help. I also had it schedule a hair appt and massage for later this month. Let's go AI!

- Listed a Facebook Marketplace item and is managing the sale. I had purchased a wagon for my kids years ago that's been collecting dust. Grok Bot found the old listing, used the photos, and asked me what $$ I want to list at. It's going to manage the rest (wish me luck here).

Mental load unlock: Who has time to sell their old crap? I sure don't. But AI has infinite time.

Notice, none of these are work examples. I will do those in a separate thread. All of these things are being done in the background, and I'm only being asked to approve or provide the AI direction. Don't be intimidated! Literally, if you've used WhatsApp or iMessage you can use Grok Bot with NO TRAINING.

AMA I'm blown away by this tech. Photo is of my home assistant (her name is Helen) independently ordering my kindergartner a photo from Walgreens that mama somehow forgot about. Oops.
